entities.summary: Euhemerus was a Greek mythographer at the court of Cassander, the king of Macedon. He was born in either Messina in Sicily or Chios, but the exact location of his birth is disputed. Euhemerus' father was Theodoros, a local chieftain, and his mother was a noblewoman named Andromeda. Euhemerus was educated in the traditional Greek arts and sciences, including philosophy, literature, and music, and he became a skilled writer and storyteller. He was known for his ability to weave together mythological and historical accounts, creating a new genre of narrative that would influence later writers such as Lucian of Samosata. Euhemerus' most famous work is the 'Pherecrates', a collection of stories about the Greek hero Pherecrates, which was widely read and admired in ancient Greece. He also wrote a treatise on the mythology of the Greeks, which was dedicated to Cassander. Euhemerus' legacy extends beyond his own writings, as his work helped to shape the way people thought about mythology and the role of the gods in human life. His influence can be seen in the works of later writers, including the Roman poet Martial, who credited Euhemerus as a model for his own narrative style. Euhemerus' story is also significant because it highlights the complex and often fraught relationship between mythology and history in ancient Greece. Despite his importance, Euhemerus' life and work are not well documented, and much of what we know about him comes from later accounts and references in other texts.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Euhemerus was a significant figure in ancient Greek literature and helped to shape the way people thought about mythology and the role of the gods in human life. His work influenced later writers and helped to establish the importance of narrative in ancient Greek culture.
